rule: Four open clauses of the campaign's success criteria were blocked on a ruling no implementation lane may write, and that fact was scattered across a report section, three escalation ledgers and a verify-ledger note. Scattered, it reads as four lanes each explaining why it stopped. Collected, it is one list with a length: these are the decisions the campaign owed itself, and nothing below closed by anybody trying harder. Every row names the criterion it blocked, the artifact carrying the measurement, the question in one sentence, and what a lane may NOT do instead -- because the second half is what keeps 'blocked on a ruling' from becoming the place work goes to stop. The first four were answered on 2026-08-14 by dated amendments in the umbrella; the rows moved to answered[] rather than being deleted, so the question, its measurement and its answer stay joined. A fifth was opened the same day, by the pass that closed the other four: a criterion cannot be discharged by the lane that discovers it is unmet. A sixth was opened by the pass that docketed the standing dissents, for the same reason and from the other end -- the one debt whose remedy is not an investigation, found by asking what a fresh investigator would be asked and finding no question; it was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment J, which adjudicates such a string by source assertion, and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. A seventh was opened on the same day by the pass that sized the fourteen receipt-walk deferrals into slices: three of them name a retiring act the campaign's own criterion 8 forbids, which is a mis-description of a debt rather than a debt anybody can pay. The seventh was answered on 2026-08-15 by Amendment K, which rules the retiring act per LANE rather than per walk -- the interpreter in the family's own declared serving lane, which is the receipt walk for eleven of the rows and the defence resolver for the three whose via says so -- and its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. An eighth was opened on 2026-08-16 by the retirement lane that measured a family with no pair row to stamp, and answered the same day by Amendment O, which rules such a family PAIR_ONLY under the umbrella's own semantic-authority rule and closes its receipt-walk row as a schedule category error rather than a retirement -- with a machine check that reopens it, and with a one-pass triage of every remaining row so the sixth lane does not rediscover what stopped the fifth; its row moved to answered[] rather than being deleted. That leaves one row open, and it is the first one: whether criterion 11's first clause binds the campaign backwards.
how_a_row_closes: The ruling is recorded in docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md -- in the [H] table, in a decision row, or as a dated amendment, which is where Amendments A through D already live -- and the row moves to answered[] naming the amendment. A row does NOT close by a lane deciding the question is smaller than it looked, and it does not close by the criterion being re-read more weakly: umbrella criterion 11's own words are that a phase document may not write its own descope.
why_a_lane_may_not_write_these: Umbrella criterion 11: every [H] is either answered and recorded in the umbrella or its dependent slice is explicitly descoped there with its criterion restated -- a phase document may not write its own descope. The same reasoning reaches a success criterion an implementation would have to reinterpret to satisfy. Amendments A, B, C and D are the precedent: each was measured by a lane, refused by that lane, and recorded in the umbrella by its owner.

owed.blocks: runbook criterion 11's first clause -- every slice has a recorded verify-<slice> verdict
owed.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/verify-ledger.json, coverage block, gated by tests/test_verify_ledger.py
owed.question: The clause has a machine denominator now and fails it backwards: 68 slice-group tags derived from commit subjects, one covered by a verdict recorded in this ledger, seven more citing a verdict in their own commit bodies with a sha a reader can open, and 61 citing nothing anywhere. R-35 was real and used -- the campaign answered NOT DISCHARGED verdicts by name -- but the verdicts were written into commit bodies rather than into an artifact, so most of them are unrecoverable as records. Does the clause bind the campaign's own past, in which case somebody schedules 61 fresh R-35 passes over closed ranges; or is it discharged forwards, by a ledger whose gate refuses the next slice group that ships without a verdict row or an explicit line?
owed.why_no_lane_may_answer_it: Both ways out are a lane deciding what a criterion means. Reading it forwards is a re-reading of 'every slice', which criterion 11's own words forbid a phase document from doing; reading it backwards commits somebody to sixty-one verification passes, which is a scheduling decision with a cost and an owner.
owed.what_a_lane_may_not_do_instead: Three things, and each has been available and refused. Manufacture a verdict for a slice nobody verified -- that is precisely the unverifiable claim about the past Phase 1 outlaws. Reconstruct verdicts from the commit bodies of the very lanes being checked, which is a record derived from the thing it is supposed to check independently. And shrink the denominator by declaring some tags 'not really slices', which is driving a counter to zero by editing what it counts.
owed.consequence_of_leaving_it_open: The clause holds forwards and is measured backwards. The gate refuses the next slice group that ships with neither a verdict row nor an explicit line, so the residue is a number that cannot grow in silence; what it does not do is fall. What preparation changed is the cost of the branch, not the choice: whoever rules may now read the exact passes the backwards reading buys, one row each, instead of an estimate.
owed.what_a_lane_may_do_and_has_done: Price the branch it may not choose. The backwards reading commits somebody to a number of fresh R-35 passes, and until 2026-08-14 that number was an estimate over a population nobody had turned into work: no commit range, no criteria locator and no brief existed for a single one of them. docs/receipts/verify-backlog.json, gated by tests/test_verify_backlog.py, is one prepared row per residue group -- the commits it spans by subject, the plan documents its stated completion criteria live in, and R-35's brief read from the runbook rather than copied, so a prepared pass cannot be handed a weakened one. This is a statement about the QUESTION a verifier would be asked and never about the answer, which is the same line the standing-dissent docket draws. It does not narrow the ruling: both branches remain exactly as written, and the row set is asserted equal to the ledger's own residue list so preparation cannot become redefinition.

owed.blocks: umbrella criterion 7's combat_state/receipt_walk deferral and, identically, opening_defense/receipt_walk and threshold_defense/receipt_walk -- the three of Amendment F's fourteen whose ruled retiring act is already performed and whose rows still cannot leave
owed.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/expected-golden-diff-campaign-close-combat-state-retirement.json, the measurement filed by the slice that stopped, beside docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json which sizes the row and publishes already_performed: true for it
owed.question: Amendment K rules the retiring act for every one of the fourteen rows to be a per-family interpreter in the family's OWN declared serving lane, and for these three that lane is defense_resolver rather than receipt_walk. INTERPRETERS has held all three of those keys since before the closeout opened, so the ruled act is performed. The deferral row is a different object: scripts/behavior_frontier.py derives counter 4's rows from interpreters.uninterpreted_pairs(), so combat_state/receipt_walk retires when and only when that pair leaves that tuple, which an interpreter registered in another lane does not do and cannot do. So what retires it? Either the receipt-walk lane declaration comes out of _FAMILY_LANES on the measured ground that the family's delivery is performed in the lane it declares -- an Amendment O, Ruling 1 shaped act on a different ground, owing its own machine check and its own reopening condition -- or the rows close on some further ground the umbrella names, as Amendment O closed crit_profile's on a ground that was not a retirement at all.
owed.why_no_lane_may_answer_it: Both readings re-scope a debt the umbrella sized. Amendment F sizes the receipt-walk debt, Amendment K settles the lane each row is spelled in and refuses in three places to touch _FAMILY_LANES, Amendment L settles what one slice contains, and Amendment O creates the one mechanism that removes a lane declaration while measuring these three families out of its class in the same paragraph -- 'Ruling 1 closes one row and not six'. Choosing between the readings is a lane deciding what its own criterion means, which umbrella criterion 11's own words forbid a phase document from doing, and D-40 forbids the edit itself from inside the counter it moves.
owed.what_a_lane_may_not_do_instead: Three things, each available and each refused by the stopped slice. Register (COMBAT_STATE, RECEIPT_WALK) with an interpreter emitting the fields the resolver already writes, which is the second producer of one number D-60 and umbrella criterion 8 forbid and which Amendment K refuses in its own words as an interpreter emitting fields nothing consumes. Drop the receipt-walk lane from _FAMILY_LANES on Amendment O, Ruling 1's authority, when that ruling requires every declaration to name Subject.HOLDER and all seven of this family's payloads carry no subject at all. And treat the performed act as the retirement, which the committed schedule answers in its own words under what_already_performed_does_not_mean.
owed.consequence_of_leaving_it_open: Three of the nine open rows stand, overdue and gated, with their blockers unchanged and their populations enumerated -- combat_state at 2648 leaves across six covering rosters -- so a lane that picks any of them up starts from a measurement rather than from a fresh discovery. What the open row costs is a distinction a reader needs and the frontier does not draw: six of the nine remaining rows are startable today by the ruled act and are unstarted only because nobody has budgeted them, and these three are not startable at all. Budget buys the six; only a ruling buys these three.

answered.amendment: Amendment E — 2026-08-14, how a disposition transition is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A disposition transition is adjudicated BY CITATION, not by verdict, under three guards: the diff must be on a dispositions entry as the identity-keyed leaf_report classifies it; the cited ruling must be one a reader can open; and the leaf the entry describes may not move. The third guard is this amendment's own contribution -- citation can only ever excuse a change in what a payload SAYS ABOUT a number that did not change.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 1's emission clause, and umbrella criterion 7's Amendment B exit clause behind it
answered.question: When publishing a refused row's outcome as STRUCTURAL_ZERO turns a disposition string from one campaign spelling into another, R-15 classifies the diff as a text_change and R-19 sends every qualifying one to an oracle -- but R-18's export is exactly data/ and docs/math-foundations.md, so no investigator can be briefed on a question about this campaign's own disposition vocabulary. Is such a leaf adjudicated by citation, the way the 2026-08-14 R-15 amendment adjudicates a membership transition that is the ruled consequence of a declared change, or does the emission need a different landing shape entirely?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The emission slice: the receipt view publishes a refused transition's outcome fields as StructuralZero carrying the walk's own refusal, landing against the committed coupled baseline plus one committed allowlist under R-17, owing no oracle receipt. Umbrella criterion 1's emission clause.

answered.amendment: Amendment G — 2026-08-14, D-25's one catch names a class
answered.the_ruling: D-25's “exactly one catch” is a rule about WHERE, never a count of the exception types that one handler names. The write-once ledger's raises are STARVED -- a record holding two answers for one question cannot answer either -- so the invariant table owes no fifth spelling. ProjectionStarvation's base is that class, the ledger's raises join it, the one boundary converts the base, and the source assertion allowlisting exactly one handler is unchanged in force.
answered.blocks: nothing yet -- it is a live operational risk rather than an unmet criterion
answered.question: Since the ledger join, OutcomeRewritten and DuplicateApplied are reachable on /api/calculate, /api/bis and /api/optimize, and the request boundary names only ProjectionStarvation. Does D-25's 'exactly one catch' name that exception specifically, or the class of programming errors a projection or a ledger raises on a request? If the class, does STARVED cover a rewritten outcome or does the invariant table owe a fifth spelling?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The boundary slice: the class of programming errors that surface as a STARVED leaf gets a name, the ledger's write-once raises join it, and the one request-boundary handler converts the base -- so a contested number is a named 500 carrying a receipt instead of a bare one.

answered.amendment: Amendment H — 2026-08-14, a leaf's own adjudicating receipt
answered.the_ruling: Criterion 4 carves out a leaf's own adjudicating receipt on three conditions: the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, it names the leaf by its path, and it agrees with the committed receipt or declares in the same artifact what it supersedes. A quotation at its address is the opposite of a second home; a second home is a figure a reader cannot trace.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 4's non-plan half, and runbook criterion 2's sole-home conjunct
answered.question: Criterion 4 says no receipt or commit body states a golden shape count of a committed baseline. The fingerprint counters are themselves leaves of the snapshot, so R-19 forces an oracle receipt adjudicating one to state it, R-17 forces an allowlist claiming one to state both sides, and R-34 forces a baseline-move commit to give a line of cause per moved value. Does criterion 4 carve out a leaf's own adjudicating receipt, or does the snapshot shape change so the counters are not compared leaves at all?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: Nothing to implement -- the residue was already measured and gated. What closes is the criterion: the eleven sites are the carve-out rather than eleven violations, and sole_home_scan.py --check keeps a twelfth from arriving.

answered.amendment: Amendment I — 2026-08-14, this criterion's frontend change budget
answered.the_ruling: The clause is amended to what shipped and gains the property the integer was reaching for: every commit in the campaign range touching static/js/app.js is named in the umbrella with its reason, and a commit that is not named is a budget overrun. bf4a6d3, 44331c7 and f25dcfa are named.
answered.question: Criterion 1 says static/js/app.js takes exactly one budgeted change at S9. Three commits in the campaign range touch it -- bf4a6d3 (+26), 44331c7 (+52/-10, the withheld marker the clause names) and f25dcfa (+13/-5, a row-classification refactor). Is the budget clause amended to what shipped, or are the two unbudgeted commits reverted?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: Nothing to implement, and deliberately so: reverting shipped rendering behaviour to satisfy a budget sentence is the ordering this campaign exists to invert. What closes is the clause, which now names commits instead of counting them.

answered.amendment: Amendment J — 2026-08-15, how a campaign-authored justification string is adjudicated
answered.the_ruling: A campaign-authored justification string that asserts a fact about src-level vocabulary is adjudicated BY SOURCE ASSERTION -- a machine check binding the string to the predicate that produces it -- and never by an R-18 investigation, whose export excludes src/ by design. An oracle verdict on such a string is valid only for its export-verifiable portion, so a verdict that turns on a vocabulary its own limitations block declares out of bounds does not sustain a dissent; and the string MAY assert the src-vocabulary fact, because the machine check is what keeps it true. Three guards: one named producing site rather than a hand list, a check total over what the sentence quantifies over and in both directions, and nothing carved out but the src-vocabulary claim -- whatever such a string asserts about the cached corpus stays R-18's.
answered.blocks: R-19's blocking half for one member of the standing-dissent population -- the open debt on oracle-P3-3.8-leaf24, which the docket routes here because it is the one debt no investigation can clear
answered.question: A coverage reason is a sentence this campaign wrote about why an item's mechanic is out of the scored functional's scope. Phase 3 reworded one; R-15 classified the reword a text_change; R-19 sent it to an investigator whose export is data/ and docs/math-foundations.md. The investigator checked both sentences against the cached corpus, found the operative claim supported on BOTH sides, and certified the old value -- because R-19's closed verdict set has no member for 'both are true and the evidence tree does not rank them'. Amendment E answered exactly this shape for a disposition string by ruling that citation adjudicates it, and said in its own words that it does not widen past the dispositions map. Is a campaign-authored justification string adjudicated by citation on the same reasoning, or does R-19's verdict set gain a member for a leaf the export cannot rank?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The one docketed dissent no investigation could clear. oracle-P3-3.8-leaf24.json stands exactly as filed and is answered rather than superseded; its open_debt row closes as a citation naming Amendment J, the docket cluster routed here leaves clusters[] by being answered, and the twenty-three-receipt majority is not re-rolled. Nothing in src/ and no baseline moves. What lands is the ruling's premise made enforceable: the source assertion binding the published sentence to item_coverage.declares_only_defence, over every cached item and in both directions, so the day the defence group changes under the sentence a gate goes red rather than a receipt going stale.

answered.amendment: Amendment K — 2026-08-15, the retiring act is named per lane, not per walk
answered.the_ruling: The retiring act for every one of the fourteen (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral rows is a per-family interpreter in the family's OWN DECLARED SERVING LANE -- RECEIPT_WALK for the eleven the pair engine feeds, DEFENSE_RESOLVER for the three the resolver feeds, and in general whichever lane that row's via names. Amendment F's act is neither narrowed nor widened; what is corrected is the lane it was spelled with, which was read off eleven rows and written over fourteen. One property is discharged either way and it is criterion 8's own: the family's numbers reach the walk through exactly one interpreter, in the lane the family declares, instead of arriving already priced by the pair engine -- so the act serves D-60 rather than colliding with it, because a resolver interpreter is not a second producer of one number, it is the one producer. delta_amp is answered by the same sentence: its structured via is pair_engine, so its ruled act is a receipt-walk interpreter, and prose naming a second route does not move a gated declaration (D-40). Three refusals ride the ruling: no interpreter is registered that emits fields nothing consumes, _FAMILY_LANES is not touched so counter 4 still counts all three, and Amendment F's fourteen are not read as eleven. The rows' recorded retiring stage is refreshed from 'Phase 4 S3 -- one kernel, five views', which Amendment F measured cannot perform the act, to this closeout, dated and citing Amendment F; re-dating changes what the rows are overdue AGAINST and nothing about whether they are overdue.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 7, through Amendment F's restatement of the fourteen receipt-walk deferrals -- three of which name an act the campaign's own criterion 8 forbids
answered.question: Amendment F restates the fourteen (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferrals as fourteen slices and names one retiring act for all of them: a per-family receipt-walk interpreter, on 'the families whose numbers participant_timeline._pair_run_fight produces today'. Measured against the frontier's own via field, eleven declare that route and three -- combat_state, opening_defense, threshold_defense -- declare the defence resolver instead, with their rows saying in their own words that a walk-lane interpreter there 'would be a second producer of one number'. That is what D-60 and umbrella criterion 8 forbid, so for those three the named retiring act is the act the campaign rules out. What retires them: an interpreter the criterion forbids, a lane-table correction saying the receipt walk never owed this family its own answer, or something else -- and does the same answer reach delta_amp, whose structured route says pair_engine while its own reason names a second route and says neither is the rule?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The three sized slices that could not start. combat_state, opening_defense and threshold_defense now carry a settled retiring act naming the interpreter in their own declared lane, so the schedule routes nothing to an owed ruling and the fourteenth row is startable on the same basis as the first. What it deliberately did NOT unblock is the debt: INTERPRETERS already holds the three (family, DEFENSE_RESOLVER) keys, so for those three the ruled act is already performed and the one-engine property is discharged today -- a fact about the tree and not permission to stop counting. All fourteen rows stand, overdue and gated, the machine still refuses a fifteenth, and the eleven are still eleven slices no phase has budgeted.

answered.amendment: Amendment O — 2026-08-16, authority reclassification, and the triage of every remaining row
answered.the_ruling: Both readings the question offered are refused and a third is ruled. Ruling 1: under the umbrella's own semantic-authority rule -- all-pair-local inputs => PAIR_ONLY -- a family whose mechanics author no pair row and fold only into the holder's OWN champion rows is PAIR_ONLY, so the pair engine is its authoritative home, no second engine prices it and no double-count exists. Its (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral row was a schedule CATEGORY ERROR rather than a debt, and it closes as not_a_gap by authority reclassification -- a different act from a retirement, with a different receipt, unavailable to a family that authors a row, and carrying a MACHINE CHECK: the zero-authored-rows property is measured over the covering population by a derived test and the row REOPENS if a future mechanic of the family ever authors one. crit_profile closes that way. Amendment F's fourteen are not read as thirteen: one row leaves as mis-scheduled and says so, which is a correction to the schedule and not a discount on the debt. Ruling 2: before any further retirement round every remaining open row is measured once for the same property and classified -- (a) authors-own-rows retires by the ruled act, (b) pair-local fold into holder-own rows closes by Ruling 1, (c) roster-relevant fold requires a NAMED walk-side delivery term in Amendment M's shape and stops the next round by name if it lacks one -- with the measurement derived, committed to the schedule receipt and diff-gated.
answered.blocks: umbrella criterion 7's crit_profile/receipt_walk deferral, and behind it Amendment F's fourteen -- the first of them whose ruled retiring act names a thing the family does not have
answered.measurement_artifact: docs/receipts/expected-golden-diff-campaign-close-crit-profile-retirement.json, the measurement filed by the slice that stopped, beside docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json which sizes the row
answered.question: Amendment L, Ruling 1 rules a retirement act as one behaviour slice carrying both halves at once -- the family's pair rows stamped pair_preview_of and declared THEORETICAL, and the lane interpreter wired to the from-declaration pricing path -- and both halves name a pair row the family authors. crit_profile authors none. Measured over both covering scenarios and over each of its three owners alone, ranged and melee: infinity_edge.crit_damage_bonus is a multiplier folded into the champion's own auto_attacks row, navori_flickerblade.cooldown_refund authors no damage at all, and sundered_sky.forced_crit authors one row carrying informational: true that is summed into no total. The one family already retired without a stamp, delta_amp, was legal because Amendment M, Ruling 1 NAMED its walk-side delivery -- the holder's static amps, which every DeclaredPacket the walk prices consumes -- and measured here the pricing stage has no crit term and none of the 17 previewed rows the committed coupled scenarios author carries a crit split, so there is no term for a crit_profile interpreter to deliver. Does a family whose numbers are folded into another family's row retire by some act this campaign has not yet named; or is its deferral row closed on a different ground than a retirement, in which case somebody says which ground and what it does to Amendment F's count of fourteen?
answered.what_the_ruling_unblocked: The row itself, and the nine behind it. crit_profile/receipt_walk is closed as not_a_gap with a derived machine check that reopens it, so the family that could not be retired is no longer a debt nobody could pay or discharge. Every remaining row now carries a measured class instead of an unmeasured assumption: four author their own rows and retire by the ruled act, five fold into rows they do not author, and one of those five -- damage_routing -- has no named walk-side delivery term anywhere in the tree or in an amendment, so the next retirement round stops there by name rather than by a sixth lane rediscovering the shape that stopped the fifth. What it deliberately did NOT unblock is the debt: nine rows stand, overdue and gated, and none of them is budgeted.

why_the_answered_rows_stay: A closed row keeps its question, its measurement artifact and what the ruling unblocked. Deleting it would leave the amendment standing in the umbrella with no record of what it was answering, which is the shape -- a conclusion whose question nobody can recover -- this campaign spent four hundred commits removing.
